question: Should OpenClaw add a core cross-gateway session messaging contract now, and should that be the narrow `gateway.peers` session-tool shape from #43656 or part of the broader federation design in #87733?
rationale: The request changes Gateway trust boundaries, config surface, session addressing, message delivery, and authorization semantics, which cannot be safely resolved by automated repair alone.

options.title: Design-first core contract
options.body: Keep this issue open, use #87733 to settle peer identity, scopes, replay, visibility, and history semantics, then repair or replace #43656 against that contract.

options.title: Narrow peer map now
options.body: Approve the `gateway.peers` direction and require #43656 or a replacement PR to preserve URL allowlisting, spawn semantics, upgrade safety, and real multi-gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Plugin or bridge route
options.body: Declare native session-tool routing out of scope and document an external MCP/plugin bridge path only if maintainers accept that it will not provide Gateway-owned session semantics.

recommendation.title: Design-first core contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, use #87733 to settle peer identity, scopes, replay, visibility, and history semantics, then repair or replace #43656 against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history trail for session tools and Gateway URL security points to steipete, and the decision spans those exact surfaces.
